items.action: Update every iPhone still on iOS 26 and every Mac on Tahoe/Sequoia immediately (Settings > General > Software Update). Treat any pre-27 device handling crafted files as at risk.
items.details: CVE-2026-86950, CVSS 8.8. Only one security fix ships in these point releases; iOS 27.0.1 was released the same day with no published CVEs since the attack targeted pre-27 builds.
items.summary: Apple released iOS 26.7.1, iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 fixing an out-of-bounds write in CoreGraphics that Apple says was used in 'extremely sophisticated' targeted attacks against devices on iOS versions before iOS 27. The flaw, reported by Meta Product Security, allows arbitrary code execution via a maliciously crafted file.
items.title: Apple patches exploited CoreGraphics zero-day (CVE-2026-86950)

items.action: If you or colleagues use Muse, keep the app updated and review which personal accounts and data you have connected to the agent.
items.details: The Information reported the flaw on Sep 26 from an internal Meta incident report; Reuters/ET CISO covered it Sep 29. Meta did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.
items.summary: An outside researcher, via Meta's bug bounty program, found a vulnerability in Meta's personal AI agent Muse that could have let an attacker access a user's dedicated cloud VM — including emails and files. Meta classified it internally as SEV-2 (third-highest severity) and is rolling out a clearer safety warning inside the app.
items.title: Meta adds safety warning to Muse AI agent after researcher found VM-access flaw

items.action: If you run self-hosted TeamCity, patch or install JetBrains' security plugin now and hunt for signs of agent-polling exploitation; block internet exposure of the server UI.
items.details: The flaw was privately reported to JetBrains on July 10, 2026 under coordinated disclosure; the ransomware-exploitation update is dated September 28. JetBrains' fully managed cloud service is already patched.
items.summary: A September 28 update to the Health-ISAC advisory confirms ransomware groups are now exploiting CVE-2026-63077, an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in JetBrains TeamCity On-Premises' agent polling protocol that lets remote attackers bypass auth and run OS commands on the server. Shadowserver still tracks 160+ unpatched customer-managed servers.
items.title: Ransomware crews now exploiting critical TeamCity RCE (CVE-2026-63077)

items.details: Cyberthreatintelligence.net aggregates these disclosures from public ransomware leak sites via the ransomware.live API; disclosure dates reflect leak-site publication, not the date of initial compromise.
items.summary: Safepay, among the most active ransomware groups this year, listed the Netherlands agri-food firm eagroep.com and the Swiss healthcare company bio-strath.com on its dark-web leak site on September 28. Healthcare listings carry maximum payment pressure given patient-data sensitivity and regulatory exposure.
items.title: Safepay ransomware claims two victims on Sep 28 (eagroep.com, bio-strath.com)

items.details: Panzer typically uses a double-extortion model — treat the listing as data-theft exposure, not just encryption.
items.summary: Healthcare target SMCare appeared on Panzer ransomware's leak site on September 28. Beyond the listing itself, no victim detail has been published, but double-extortion means stolen data may be published if demands are not met.
items.title: Panzer ransomware claims healthcare target SMCare

items.details: Both claims are leak-site disclosures aggregated from public sources; compromise dates and impact remain unconfirmed.
items.summary: Emperador ransomware published two leak-site listings on September 28: Brazilian tech firm Amazon Informatica and SiteProRentals. Technology-sector targets are valuable for intellectual property and customer data, with possible downstream supply-chain exposure.
items.title: Emperador ransomware lists Amazon Informatica and SiteProRentals

items.action: Update Microsoft 365 Apps and Office LTSC 2021/2024 to the latest security builds; treat unexpected attachments with suspicion.
items.details: The vulnerability is linked to how Outlook handles certain inputs; a specially designed file or message can trigger arbitrary code execution. Affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and Office LTSC 2021/2024, 32-bit and 64-bit.
items.summary: CERT-In's vulnerability note dated September 28 flags a high-severity remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-70125) in Microsoft 365 apps, particularly Outlook. Successful exploitation could let a remote attacker run harmful code on the affected computer and take control of parts of the system.
items.title: CERT-In issues high-severity warning for Microsoft Outlook flaw (CVE-2026-70125)

items.details: The Asia-Pacific region recorded 143 victims (13% of the global total); India, Thailand, Taiwan and Japan accounted for 68 of them, nearly half.
items.summary: August was the most active ransomware month of 2026 so far, with 1,034 organisations named by 88 gangs worldwide — up 25% from July. India emerged as the most-targeted country in Asia-Pacific with 24 claimed victims, ranking seventh worldwide; manufacturing (151) and IT/ITES (126) were the hardest-hit sectors.
items.title: India was APAC's most-targeted ransomware country in August — Cyble CRIL report

items.details: Doommageddon uses public leak sites to pressure victims; defenders should watch for unauthorized network access and verify backup and recovery procedures.
items.summary: Chem Process Systems Pvt. Ltd. was listed on Doommageddon ransomware's leak site on September 28, with a deadline of October 5, 2026 set for potential publication of stolen data. The attack vector, data volume, and operational impact remain unconfirmed.
items.title: Doommageddon ransomware lists India's Chem Process Systems Pvt. Ltd.

items.details: The arrests follow Supreme Court directions to investigate major 'digital arrest' scam cases; police have secured around Rs 44 lakh so far in a linked Lucknow case by placing liens on suspect accounts.
items.summary: The CBI arrested Himanshu Prasad and Unis Biswas in coordinated raids across 22 locations in 10 states under Operation Chakra-VI. The network allegedly siphoned Rs 11.4 crore from a Gujarat victim held under 'digital arrest' for three months by criminals impersonating police and TRAI officials.
items.title: CBI arrests 2 in Rs 11.4-crore 'digital arrest' scam under Operation Chakra-VI
